chunks: Zurarah narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said:
"The salat (prayer) is not repeated except for five things: taharah (ritual purity), the time, the qiblah, the rukuʿ, and the sujud."
Then he said: "The recitation is a sunnah (prophetic tradition), and the tashahhud is a sunnah (prophetic tradition), and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) does not invalidate the obligatory act."

The general rule regarding forgetfulness is that whoever forgets in the first two rakʿahs of every salat (prayer), then repetition is upon him; and whoever doubts in the Maghrib prayer, then repetition is upon him; and whoever doubts in the Ghadat prayer, then repetition is upon him.

And whoever doubts in the Jumuʿah prayer, then repetition is upon him. And whoever doubts between the second and third, or between the third and fourth, takes the greater number; then when he gives salām, he completes what he thinks has been omitted.

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدُ: the testimony portion in prayer, treated here as sunnah
key_terms.الطَّهُورِ: ritual purity required for the validity of prayer
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction toward which one prays
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةُ: the recitation in prayer, treated here as sunnah

ai.seo_question: When must salat (prayer) be repeated due to forgetfulness or doubt according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out key legal principles regarding mistakes and doubt in salat (prayer). It states that the prayer is only repeated for defects in five foundational matters, while elements such as recitation and tashahhud are treated as sunnah (prophetic tradition) and do not nullify the obligatory structure of the prayer; it also outlines rulings for doubt in specific prayers and rakʿahs.
